newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Airplus sees slow growth for cargo.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Airplus sees slow growth for cargo.

text.p: Lufthansa Airplus Servicekarten GmbH said the lack of an air cargo industry electronic reservations system was holding back development of its electronic cargo payment card.
The Deutsche Lufthansa AG credit card subsidiary said it had agreed deals with only 130 companies, forwarders and express firms since launching the card last year.

Peter Metzler, Lufthansa Airplus joint managing director, told a news conference: "We expected it would be slow and we expect it will go slowly for the next two to three years because our product will first be used when the electronic systems exist."
The air cargo industry had no computer reservation system (CRS) such as the Amadeus, Galileo or Sabre systems in the passenger travel industry for electronic bookings, he explained.
"The pre-condition of a card system is the existence or a system environment between clients and suppliers," he said.
Bookings of aircraft space for air cargo shipments are currently made through a multitude of airline, forwarder and integrator in-house systems, observers noted.
With the Lufthansa Airplus Cargo Card, air cargo shippers or freight forwarders would pay a single monthly invoice for shipments with Lufthansa Cargo AG.
Use of a single payment system would also cardholders to analyse transport costs by route, by weight or other factors.
